messages:
sara: FYI ran into a weird typing mismatch when trying to use the SDK from an edge TypeScript project (Cloudflare Pages). Generics on `client.embeddings<T>()` lose their concrete shape and come through as `unknown`.
sara: repro: SDK v1.1.0-alpha, TS 5.3, bundler is esbuild via Snowpack-ish pipeline. tsconfig has declaration:true and emitDeclarationOnly for the lib build.
sara: tsconfig snippet:
```
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "module": "ESNext",
    "target": "ES2022",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler",
    "declaration": true,
    "emitDeclarationOnly": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true
  }
}
```
sara: sample usage:
```
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'
const c = createClient({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
const out = await c.embeddings<{ vector: number[] }>(["a"])
// expecting out[0].vector to be number[] but VSCode shows 'unknown'
```
tom: thanks. two quick checks: are you consuming the package's .d.ts from the ESM entrypoint or the CJS one? bundlers sometimes prefer `exports`/`types` fields differently. Can you paste your node_modules/@redwood/inference/package.json exports/types?
ben: also curious whether your declaration build (emitDeclarationOnly) is transforming conditional types to `unknown` because some types rely on lib.dom being present. Edge runtimes without DOM libs can widen types.
sara: pasted package.json snippet:
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  }
},
"types": "dist/types/index.d.ts",
```
sara: I see VSCode resolving to dist/types/index.d.ts (expected). But the d.ts file has this odd union overload set where the generic param is on one overload only, looks like our build split the overloads across files.
tom: that rings a bell. We used a pattern to provide both named and default exports with separate overloads historically. When declarations are emitted separately (emitDeclarationOnly), TS can write different overload blocks and consumers with `moduleResolution: bundler` pick the wrong overload. Short-term: try setting `moduleResolution` to `node16` or `nodeNext` or set `esModuleInterop: true` to make import resolution canonical.
ben: longer term fix in SDK: unify overloads behind a single exported interface so the declaration emitter doesn't duplicate signatures. Also add a thin re-export file at `dist/types/esm.d.ts` that references the canonical types to avoid bundlers reading partials.
sara: quick test: changed my tsconfig to moduleResolution: nodeNext and restarted TS server -> inference improved, generics now flow. Not ideal to require that for all users though.
tom: opened a small DX issue in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/422 (notes and steps). I'll add a types-only PR that keeps backward compat: export a `TypedEmbeddings<T>` helper type and add a single entry point for `types` in package.json.
ben: added a draft PR branch: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/789 (types-only changes). includes change to rollup plugin to emit a single `index.d.ts` with consolidated overloads and a tiny README note for edge users.
tom: CI types checker passed locally. types-bot: running full typesuite on PR/789
sara: for anyone hitting this now: workaround options
- set compilerOptions.moduleResolution to "nodeNext" or "node16"
- set esModuleInterop: true and use default import `import createClient from '@redwood/inference'`
- explicitly cast the call `as EmbeddingResponse<{vector:number[]}>`
sara: will try to validate PR branch with our Pages deployment later today and report back.
types-bot: PR/789: types-only check queued 947
sara: thanks all, saved me a lot of head-scratching. filing a small internal note for onboarding checklist so support folks know this edge-case for ESM/emitDeclarationOnly pipelines.
